positioning.category: AI-native model release foundry for JavaScript and WebGPU
positioning.initialIcp: TypeScript/Electron desktop products on Windows and macOS
positioning.northStar: Production model releases whose eligibility decision is delegated to Doppler and relied upon by the customer’s activation system.
positioning.promise: Give Doppler a pinned model, Electron application revision, acceptance suite, supported-device policy, previous release, rollout rules, and rollback target; receive a signed eligible-or-blocked production release decision and its immutable evidence bundle.
positioning.buyer: TypeScript teams shipping Electron desktop products on Windows and macOS.

architecture.invariant: After a Pack is qualified and signed, Runtime may not change its semantic graph, kernel closure, dtype lane, fusion strategy, quantization policy, or memory model.

commercialOffer.name: Doppler Production Release
commercialOffer.promise: Qualify one pinned model revision for one pinned Electron application revision and return a signed eligible-or-blocked recommendation, immutable Pack, qualification evidence, exclusions, and customer-controlled rollback target.
intake: pinned upstream model revision, tokenizer, weights, configuration, and license
pinned Electron application revision, acceptance tests, workload identity, and oracle identity
supported Windows and macOS device policy with exact Electron, GPU, and driver constraints
eligible incumbent controls and declared correctness class
privacy, artifact distribution, hardware, memory, latency, and recovery constraints
previous release, rollout rules, and rollback target
deliverables: source-derived ModelIR and retained conversion provenance
signed immutable Pack with qualified TargetPlans
Windows and macOS Electron fleet qualification receipts for declared tuples
application-owned correctness, lifecycle, reliability, memory, and performance evidence
signed eligible-or-blocked promotion recommendation that never activates the application
known exclusions and typed rejection reasons
failure bundle, previous working Pack, rollback target, and revocation configuration
commercialOffer.promotionGate: An external customer’s activation system relies on Doppler’s eligible-or-blocked decision for a production release and its subsequent upgrade while retaining activation and rollback authority.

referenceIntegrations.classification: Internally controlled reference integrations proving application-integration mechanics.

promotionSequence.gate: The validated contract and goal matrix name Doppler Production Release, Doppler Release Operations, the Electron ICP, and the customer-controlled activation boundary.
production-release/v1 freezes one Electron document-search reranker upgrade as non-commercial acceptance evidence.
All seven Pack release requirements are immutable, validated, typed, hash-bound, and rejection-tested.
The reference reranking workload executes only through Pack validation, qualified TargetPlan selection, execution, and evidence.
doppler release consumes one production-release/v1 manifest and emits the complete non-promoting release bundle.
A typed Electron adapter and customer-operated Windows and macOS qualification agents retain exact device receipts.
A reusable GitHub Action orchestrates external fleet receipts and emits a signed recommendation without deployment or self-promotion authority.
Revocation authority is production-qualified and customer-controlled rollback is exercised against atomic durable release state.
One paid external customer relies on Doppler eligibility for a production release and the subsequent upgrade.
Two additional unrelated customers repeat the production release path.

dataCustody.defaultRule: Customer-private models, inputs, outputs, and application facts remain isolated unless explicit authority grants a narrower use.

acquisitionBoundary.operatingObjective: Production model releases whose eligibility decision is delegated to Doppler and relied upon by the customer’s activation system.
acquisitionBoundary.rule: Acquisition leverage is a possible consequence of external release dependence, never the substitute for building it.

forbiddenInferences: A valid Pack does not establish application support.
A runtime proof does not establish complete Pack-first surface convergence.
One internal model conversion does not establish a commercial release platform.
Provider availability does not authorize runtime invention or fallback.
Valera consumption or Doe execution does not define Doppler's standalone survival.
